sections.title: Form and colour
sections.text: Rusty bog-moss is a fine, compact species, usually orange-brown to dark brown, with small shoots packed into dense hummocks. British field observations describe hummocks commonly up to about 50 cm high and 75 cm across, though larger examples occur.

sections.title: Habitat and distinction
sections.text: It is characteristic of acidic, often nutrient-poor bogs, where it can build hummocks above the surrounding surface. Its compact brown cushions in the plate fit this habit; brown Sphagnum species can still be difficult to distinguish without close examination.

sections.title: Use and safety
sections.text: It contributes to peat formation and water storage. It is not a food plant, and wild collection can harm slow-forming peatland habitats.
